correctness.rationale: The normal spectral theorem yields the exact maximum of two real-part-square functions. A direct trigonometric expansion identifies the difference as -A+B cos(2t-phi), B²=A²+U²; the positive-part arc integral is exactly (U-A arctan(U/A))/pi. Degenerate cases are handled without division by zero. Strict phase monotonicity and radial pointwise domination prove the equality cases. Taylor expansion proves the precise cubic coefficient for 0<s<r and linear response for r=s. 216 deterministic finite quadrature checks from the standalone code passed; they are supplementary only.

The proposed surviving result is the exact angular second moment for all normal two-point spectra with arbitrary unequal nonzero radii, together with phase extrema and a sharp cubic-to-linear radial collision law.
